# A const func that reaches the host through sngl:x/gen is a producer: its
# value is stored, behind what it recorded reading and the digest of the code
# that read it -- the plugin's package and everything it imports. A store hit
# runs nothing, so it needs no grant; an edit to what was read, or to the
# plugin, is a miss.
env SNGL_GENCACHE_DIR=$WORK/store

sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html -o out --allow-command='./pc=sh' --debug app.sngl
grep 'v1: one' out/index.html
! stderr 'gencache hit" req="sngl.eval'

# Nothing changed: a hit, and no command runs, so none needs allowing.
sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html -o out --debug app.sngl
grep 'v1: one' out/index.html
stderr 'gencache hit" req="sngl.eval'

# What the plugin read changed: a miss, and the command it runs is asked about
# again.
cp data2.txt data.txt
! sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html -o out app.sngl
stderr 'may not run sh -c'
sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html -o out --allow-command='./pc=sh' app.sngl
grep 'v1: two' out/index.html

# The plugin changed, and nothing it read did: still a miss, or the old
# plugin's answer would be replayed.
sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html -o out --debug app.sngl
stderr 'gencache hit" req="sngl.eval'
cp pc2.sngl pc/pc.sngl
sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html -o out --allow-command='./pc=sh' --debug app.sngl
! stderr 'gencache hit" req="sngl.eval'
grep 'v2: two' out/index.html

# So did a package the plugin imports.
cp fmt2.sngl pc/fmt/fmt.sngl
sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html -o out --allow-command='./pc=sh' --debug app.sngl
! stderr 'gencache hit" req="sngl.eval'
grep 'v2= two' out/index.html

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import pc "./pc"

const v = pc.read("data.txt")

ui.window(title="t") {
    ui.text(value=v)
}
-- data.txt --
one
-- data2.txt --
two
-- pc/pc.sngl --
import gen "sngl:x/gen"
import f "./fmt"

// The first line of path, behind a version the command reports.
const func read(path string) string {
    var tag = ""
    var p = gen.exec(cmd=["sh", "-c", "echo v1"])
    for var line = p.stdout {
        tag = line
    }
    for var line = gen.lines(path) {
        return f.label(tag, line)
    }
    return ""
}
-- pc2.sngl --
import gen "sngl:x/gen"
import f "./fmt"

// The first line of path, behind a version the command reports.
const func read(path string) string {
    var tag = ""
    var p = gen.exec(cmd=["sh", "-c", "echo v2"])
    for var line = p.stdout {
        tag = line
    }
    for var line = gen.lines(path) {
        return f.label(tag, line)
    }
    return ""
}
-- pc/fmt/fmt.sngl --
// A tag and a value.
const func label(tag string, value string) => "{tag}: {value}"
-- fmt2.sngl --
// A tag and a value.
const func label(tag string, value string) => "{tag}= {value}"
